plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers on tall slender stems. In mild autumn climates it continues flowering until the first hard frost, attracting bees, butterflies, and hoverflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to late autumn in the Northern Hemisphere; spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Mexico; widely cultivated in gardens across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word 'kosmos' meaning 'harmony' or 'ordered universe', a name given by Spanish priests who grew them in mission gardens in Mexico.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A corm-forming perennial that sends up crocus-like lilac flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves emerge the following spring and die back by early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late autumn (September to November)
plants.location: Native to damp meadows and woodland edges across Europe; naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus and is highly toxic, containing colchicine, which is used in medicine to treat gout and is also used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Streets and parks turn purple during peak bloom, and fallen petals carpet the ground below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Sydney, Brisbane), Argentina, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and in Australia a folk belief says a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial cultivated for thousands of years that peaks in autumn as day length shortens, producing dense pompon, spider, or daisy-like blooms. It is a staple of fall gardens and festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (October to November) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Originated in China; cultivated worldwide, especially in East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants that initiate flower buds when nights lengthen, and in Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and celebrated at the Chrysanthemum Festival.
